_what: Line-keyed shot plan for the introduction film. Reviewable BEFORE recording: anchors cannot be resolved until word-level alignment exists, so shots are keyed to script line numbers, not timecodes.
_pair_claims: Every shot states the claim the image and the words make TOGETHER, as one sentence beginning 'This is telling me that'. That pairing is what no per-sentence gate can check, and it is how the Block-under-'inscribed-on-Bitcoin' error shipped in the last film.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that an ordinary penny, worn by a century of handling, is the object in question.
shots.note: Crop note permits cover-fit. No Chang context yet, so no act is implied.
shots.narration: For more than a century the penny has circulated, considered a worthless nuisance.

shots.figure: ONE CENT — the Treasury's valuation, fixed, whatever the year
shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that the Treasury's figure is a single fixed number.
shots.note: Typographic. No object image, so nothing asserts WHICH cent.
shots.narration: To the Treasury it is worth exactly one cent, whatever year it was struck, and always will be.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that the metal in a pre-1983 cent was worth about three times its face value in 2024.
shots.note: Epoch stated on screen; the essay's epoch note requires the year be visible.
shots.narration: Those struck before 1983 are copper, and in March 2024 that copper was worth about three cents.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that three different valuations attach to one and the same coin.
shots.note: a01 as the centred object. DELIBERATELY NOT a02: a02's five stacked states are TRANSFORMATIONS, and using it here would assert the three valuations are those five states.
shots.narration: Three valuations of one small object, and no two of them agree.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that Chang removed cents from circulation by hand, sorting them in bulk.
shots.note: The culling in progress — the act named by the line, not its result.
shots.narration: Recognising those discrepancies, Rutherford Chang removed ten thousand copper cents from circulation and called the work CENTS.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that he accumulated and catalogued ordinary objects over time.
shots.note: Hand-marked biro bands carry the 'time made them singular' sense without a second claim.
shots.narration: He had spent his working life collecting ordinary things until time made them singular.

shots.figure: 3,400+ copies of the same record — no two worn alike
shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that he collected over three thousand copies of one record and that each had worn differently.
shots.note: NO ASSET for the Beatles work. Typographic fallback. A penny image here would assert the records ARE pennies — do not reach for one.
shots.narration: More than three and a half thousand copies of the same Beatles record, no two worn alike.

shots.figure: New Museum, New York · Akademie der Künste, Berlin · Kunsthal Rotterdam
shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that the work was exhibited at these three institutions over twenty years.
shots.note: NO installation photography in inventory. Venue names only. The UCCA retrospective is deliberately absent: it ran Jan-Apr 2026, after his death, so naming it here would invert the chronology.
shots.narration: Shown for two decades — the New Museum in New York, the Akademie der Künste in Berlin, Kunsthal Rotterdam.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that Chang died in February 2025, the same day the order came.
shots.note: RELATION 5 RISK. A plain date card deliberately. Pairing this with a penny or the block would make the coincidence read as the work ENDING — the one thing this film must not say. No portrait of Chang in inventory.
shots.narration: He died in February 2025, at forty-five, on the day the President ordered the Treasury to stop making pennies.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that each coin was individually photographed on a copy stand, and the capture catalogued.
shots.note: THE ACT, not the result. This is the relation-4 pair the last film got wrong: a finished photograph stood in for the verb 'photographed'. Crop note: keep camera AND laptop.
shots.narration: Every one of the ten thousand was photographed first.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that the portrait on the cent is Brenner's, and that it is the most reproduced artwork on Earth.
shots.note: SUPERLATIVE. Sourced to the project's own text (essay l.15), not independently verified, and it is a claim about a set nobody can count. Inventory previously marked a06 unused for this reason. Faithful to the source of record; your call whether to keep the superlative.
shots.narration: The portrait on them, Victor David Brenner's Lincoln, is the most reproduced artwork on Earth. Two hundred and eighty-eight billion of them in existence, by the project's count in 2024.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that the project counted 288 billion Lincoln cents in existence in 2024.
shots.note: Epoch now ON SCREEN. The figure is March 2024 and the script no longer says 'still'. DO NOT use a13 here - its grid is 198 listings and would assert the grid IS the 288 billion.
shots.narration: The portrait on them, Victor David Brenner's Lincoln, is the most reproduced artwork on Earth. Two hundred and eighty-eight billion of them in existence, by the project's count in 2024.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that circulation left verdigris and wear on the coin's surface.
shots.note: Verdigris is named in the line and visible in the asset. Keep the date edge visible per crop note.
shots.narration: Circulation made the marks: verdigris, abrasion, a fingerprint, the way each one left.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that human collectors named the traits by voting, in rounds, not an algorithm.
shots.note: Now in scope — the inventory's 'not used' note described the objecthood script. Crop note: full-width band only, never scaled down.
shots.narration: No algorithm assigned any of it. The names came afterwards, from the collectors, over two years of voting.

shots.figure: more than half the set: no mark at all
shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that over half the ten thousand carry no trait, which is what gives the marked ones meaning.
shots.note: Typographic. NOT a13: showing a grid of 198 listings under 'more than half the set' would assert the grid is the set.
shots.narration: More than half the set carries no mark at all, which is what makes the rest mean anything.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that the coins were melted and poured into a mould to make one block.
shots.note: THE ACT. Crop note: never crop to the stream alone — the mould is what the copper is becoming. Max ~560px; do not full-bleed.
shots.narration: Then he destroyed them, smelted into one block of thirty-one kilograms.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that each of the ten thousand photographs was inscribed on its own satoshi.
shots.note: THE CORRECTION. This is the exact pairing the last film got wrong by showing the copper Block here. Nothing depicting the block may appear on this line.
shots.narration: Each photograph he inscribed on a satoshi, the smallest unit of Bitcoin.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that a 3D model of the block was made — a digital object, not the physical ingot.
shots.note: a05 is explicitly the DIGITAL model. Crop note: inset ≤700px, never full-bleed.
shots.narration: The block he had scanned, and inscribed as the whole of Bitcoin block 839969.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that the model's inscription filled Bitcoin block 839969 by itself.
shots.note: no_crop: the two panels ARE the content. Near full width or it is illegible.
shots.narration: The block he had scanned, and inscribed as the whole of Bitcoin block 839969.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that the physical ingot is dense and cannot be destroyed.
shots.note: NO PHOTOGRAPH of the finished physical block in inventory. a05 must NOT be used here — it is the digital model, and pairing it would equate the model with the ingot, the exact distinction the glossary forbids.
shots.narration: An ingot so dense it cannot be destroyed.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that the ten thousand were released at one satoshi each and that by October 2026 the ones listed for sale were asking around 360,000 satoshis.
shots.note: Now carries the film's only present-moment measurement. a13 is verified 2026-10-06, which IS the epoch of the second sentence - asset and claim share a date. Crop note: keep coin, id AND price; the prices are the content. Caption must say LISTED, not sold: 198 open listings, not recorded sales.
shots.narration: He released all ten thousand at one sat each. By October 2026 the ones listed for sale were asking around three hundred and sixty thousand sats.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that the set stops at 1982 because the cent stopped being copper in 1983.
shots.note: The year histogram, if built, belongs across lines 20–22.
shots.narration: The set is closed. It stops at 1982, because in 1983 the penny stopped being copper.

shots.figure: 1943 — copper to the war; the cent struck in steel
shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that 1943 is absent because that year's cent was steel, not copper.
shots.note: No 1943 steel cent in inventory. Typographic. Counted claim — 'only one of the years it misses means anything' is a claim about a set and was verified by counting.
shots.narration: Only one of the years it misses means anything. In 1943 the copper went to the war, and the cent was struck in steel.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that the set's boundaries came from the material, not from a choice.
shots.note: WEAKEST PAIRING in the plan. g01 is copper dust; it does not depict edges. Candidate for the year histogram instead. Review this one first.
shots.narration: A set with edges nobody chose.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that the final cent was struck in November 2025, as the project had anticipated.
shots.note: Quotation-tagged claim in the ledger; keep the wording exact.
shots.narration: The project had described this as coming: the last penny was struck in November 2025.

shots.pair_claim: This is telling me that the coin's states — coin, inscription, copper, block — are one continuing transformation whose value is still being decided.
shots.note: THE CLOSER. a02's stacked states are literally 'their transformation'. no_crop=True: full frame, no crop, or the sequence is lost. Ends on continuation, not on an ending.
shots.narration: Its value can continue to be redefined through this digitally scarce set of ten thousand, and the block that encapsulates their transformation.

_epoch: Shot captions carry the epoch of any time-varying figure they show. a13 is the only asset whose own verification date (2026-10-06) is load-bearing for a claim, and it is paired with the line whose epoch matches.
